packs.title: City Layers
packs.promise: Read the city through public rooms, material clues, quiet paths and movement.

q.s: Collect three clues to a civic interior.
st: Use a current open visitor period and valid applicable admission at Burg 12 (€8 general, with documented reductions or free eligibility). Check the room calendar: council and weddings can close the rooms. At Musea Brugge, under-12s need an adult. Use the free cloakroom or lockers for unsuitable bags, wet coats, umbrellas, food and drink. Only hand luggage under 34 × 22 cm are allowed, and an admitted small backpack must be carried in the hand; staff decide what may enter. Pets are not admitted to museum buildings except registered assistance dogs; bring the dog’s identification card. The Belfry has its separate no-dog rule. Keep 30 cm from exhibits, do not touch or lean on displays, and follow staff instructions. Personal photos are optional only where permitted, without flash or tripod; do not photograph identifiable staff. Normal hours 09:30–17:00, last entry 16:30. Council on the last Monday and weddings Tuesday morning, Friday afternoon or Saturday morning can close the rooms.
In the admitted civic room, collect one structural detail, one decorative detail and one labelled link to city government. Identify each by its location.
Write a sentence explaining how those three clues make the room useful or meaningful for public life. An interpretation may be uncertain; distinguish a label from your own inference.
Leave by the signed visitor route. The neighbouring Brugse Vrije is not a required extra visit.

q.s: Make an original response to the admitted space.
st: Check worship and current museum hours, then use valid applicable museum admission (€10 general or documented reduction/free category; valid €19 Gruuthuse combination also applies). Free church access does not admit the museum. Follow the pavilion and staff’s normal visitor-entry signs. At Musea Brugge, under-12s need an adult. Use the free cloakroom or lockers for unsuitable bags, wet coats, umbrellas, food and drink. Only hand luggage under 34 × 22 cm are allowed, and an admitted small backpack must be carried in the hand; staff decide what may enter. Pets are not admitted to museum buildings except registered assistance dogs; bring the dog’s identification card. The Belfry has its separate no-dog rule. Keep 30 cm from exhibits, do not touch or lean on displays, and follow staff instructions. Personal photos are optional only where permitted, without flash or tripod; do not photograph identifiable staff. Normal museum hours 09:30–17:00, Sunday 13:30–17:00, last entry 30 minutes before close; worship, weddings and funerals can change access.
From an admitted visitor position, notice one light source, one shadow edge and one spatial rhythm. Do not approach a barrier or worshipper to improve the view.
Create a short original paragraph or simple line composition connecting those three observations. It need not reproduce any artwork.
Add the place and approximate observation time. Keep voices low and leave by the current normal visitor route.

q.s: Find evidence in building, display and story.
st: On an open non-Monday use the normal Mariastraat 38 visitor entry and valid applicable admission (€15 general or documented reduction/free eligibility). Check the 30 minute last-entry cutoff. At Musea Brugge, under-12s need an adult. Use the free cloakroom or lockers for unsuitable bags, wet coats, umbrellas, food and drink. Only hand luggage under 34 × 22 cm are allowed, and an admitted small backpack must be carried in the hand; staff decide what may enter. Pets are not admitted to museum buildings except registered assistance dogs; bring the dog’s identification card. The Belfry has its separate no-dog rule. Keep 30 cm from exhibits, do not touch or lean on displays, and follow staff instructions. Personal photos are optional only where permitted, without flash or tripod; do not photograph identifiable staff. Normal hours 09:30–17:00, last entry 16:30; current holiday closures still govern.
Collect three located traces: one from the building, one from an admitted display and one from its explanation of care or hospitality. Do not assume any named object or pharmacy room is available.
Write how each trace gives different evidence. Mark your own inference separately from a label’s factual statement.
Leave by the normal visitor route to Mariastraat. Use the sidewalk over Mariabrug toward Walplein and Wijngaardstraat for the next outdoor stops.

packs.title: Sint-Anna & the North
packs.promise: Follow public streets from a lodge and craft places to a garden, rampart and museum.

q.s: Make a small original exterior study.
st: Choose an ordinary public position on Sint-Annaplein where you can see the actual church exterior without obstructing its doors. The task does not require entering the church.
Notice four relationships: a vertical edge, a horizontal edge, a repeated shape and the gap around the building.
Make four original written lines or a simple four-line sketch from those observations. Move if the square becomes busy and keep worshippers out of photos.

q.s: Collect three links in a craft.
st: Use the ordinary Balstraat 16 visitor reception on an open Monday–Saturday, before the current ticket cutoff; museum closes 17:00 and last online ticket 16:00. Use valid applicable admission (€8 general, €6 ages 12–25 or 65+, under 12 free with parents). Check holiday closures and staff rules.
In admitted displays collect a thread/material clue, a tool/action clue and a pattern clue. Locate each and use current interpretation if a process is unfamiliar.
Write how the three clues connect. A demonstration, lesson, purchase, interview or handling lace is not required.
Leave by the ordinary visitor route and return toward Jan van Eyckplein via Kantwerkstersplein, Jeruzalemstraat, Sint-Anna and the public stone bridge/Spinolarei course.

q.s: Make a short piece from what is actually here.
st: On the public Rolweg course find the signed garden visitor entry at 64 and check that it is open. Garden 09:30–17:00; 1 April–2 November closed Monday; 3 November–31 March closed Monday and Tuesday. This task uses the garden only, not the monthly house opening.
From an ordinary visitor path notice three actual textures or shapes. Choose your own words; do not copy or attribute a poem to Guido Gezelle.
Write a short original three-line piece. Stay on paths and leave through the signed visitor exit to continue along Rolweg toward Kruisvest.
